trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore every area of Leonida — 52 areas by the starter checklist's count. Exploration trophies in this series unlock per named region as you physically enter it, so the method is coverage: drive or fly every road, island and backwater at least once, and watch for the last few percent hiding in places like offshore islands, swamps or a single city district you always bypass. A helicopter or seaplane sweep is the fastest way to find the gaps once the mainland is covered. If the game fogs unexplored map, let the fog itself be your checklist.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — nine gangs by the starter checklist's count, one successful robbery apiece. The trap is repetition: robbing the same convenient gang nine times earns nothing, so track which gangs you have hit in this app and deliberately travel for the missing ones. Expect each operation to be defended; scout the site, strike fast, and leave before reinforcements turn a robbery into a siege. Gang territories should become clearer as the story names its factions, so this grind is easier after the campaign than during it.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail at a spot with a view on Ocean Beach. This is a quiet-moment trophy: find a bar, kiosk or rooftop on the Ocean Beach strip that serves drinks, order a cocktail, and let the moment play out — trophies phrased like this usually pop when the drink animation or the view prompt completes, not when you pay. If one venue does not trigger it, try another along the beach, ideally an elevated one where 'with a view' is unambiguous. It costs a few in-game dollars and a minute of patience, and nothing suggests it is tied to a story window.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom — through the glass, in a car, 'in classic style'. We flag this missable because showroom escapes in this series are signature set pieces, most often scripted inside a specific mission, and a scripted exit may not be reproducible by simply driving into a dealership in free roam. When a mission puts you inside a showroom with a car, take the dramatic exit through the front glass rather than any marked door. If free-roam showrooms do allow it, any dealership visit will do — but until that is confirmed, do not walk past the story moment expecting a second chance, and save before missions set around car businesses.

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Do the 'follow-through' at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — the series' long-running bowling joke made literal. Go to the named alley, start a game of bowling, and complete a proper follow-through on your throw; phrasing like this usually hides a simple interaction, so a full game at the named location is the safest interpretation. If a single throw does not pop it, finish the whole game — some moment trophies wait for the activity's end screen. trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The official description — 'A partnership with mass appeal' — is deliberately cryptic, and we will not pretend otherwise: it points at the two protagonists' partnership doing something crowd-pleasing, but the exact act is not stated anywhere in the trophy list. Our honest advice is to do partner activities together whenever the game offers them — hangouts, paired activities and joint free-roam feats — and to keep both characters' shared moments unskipped during the story. Hidden trophies worded this vaguely usually attach to a specific scripted beat or a repeatable partner interaction, so if it pops, note where; if you finish everything else without it, this is the one to research first once community knowledge exists. We do not flag it missable, because nothing in the text proves a one-time window.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — lots of them: the starter checklist noted PSN tracking a count toward 500 for this one. That scale means everyday decisions, not just big story branches: dialogue picks, approach choices, mercy-or-violence calls and activity selections should all feed the counter. Play decisively rather than reloading to undo outcomes, and the count builds across a normal campaign plus cleanup. Because the description never defines a 'choice', treat the PSN progress counter as the truth — check it early in your playthrough to confirm which actions move it, then lean on those. It is a marathon counter, not a skill test, so start it early and never leave it all for the end.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The description — 'Second time's the charm' — describes succeeding at something on the second attempt after failing the first. We flag it missable because fail-then-retry trophies usually attach to a specific attempt-based moment, such as a mission objective, a race or a heist step, and a one-chance story attempt may not come back. Practical approach: when the game presents a notable timed, scored or pass/fail attempt during the story, do not reload a save to erase a failure — let the failure stand, retry immediately, and succeed on the second try, which is exactly the pattern the text describes. The precise attempt it counts is not named in the official list, so this pattern-following is a reasoned reading, not a verified step; if a second-try success in free roam pops it first, so much the better.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange — the series' traditional UFO-and-weirdness trophy, hidden behind the vaguest description on the list. There is no honest step-by-step for this yet: the official text names no place, time or event. Series convention says to investigate remote spots at night — swamps, mountaintops, the ocean at odd hours — and to follow up any odd lights, sounds or stranger rumours the game plants. Treat it as a cleanup-phase curiosity: if you finish everything else first, your exploration for The Goodtime State will likely have taken you past wherever it hides. We flag no missable risk, because easter-egg witnesses in this series are repeatable world events.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — striking a pedestrian or enemy with a melee weapon from a moving vehicle, bowling-style. Use a bike or an open car, equip a melee weapon, and ride past a target at moderate speed: too slow and the swing whiffs, too fast and you simply run them over, which is a different animation and likely does not count. Crowded pavements and beach paths give you repeated chances in one pass. The description does not say the victim must be an enemy, so a single drive-by hit on any character should satisfy the wording — verify against the pop before repeating it.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 worth of Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills presumably come from robberies — banks, trucks and operations — so this trophy quietly rewards doing Maximum Withdrawal, A Classic Blitz Play and Pest Control first and routing every marked payout through the laundering contacts instead of spending it raw. Keep a running total in this tracker; a quarter-million is a campaign-scale sum, not an afternoon's work. Whether laundering pays a fee or a percentage cut is not stated in the official list, so launder in large batches to minimise trips either way.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 in total across all shops. 'Across all shops' means the spending is cumulative everywhere — clothes, weapons, ammo, vehicle work, haircuts, drinks — so the counter grows on its own if you actually use the economy instead of hoarding. Feed it deliberately during cleanup: restock ammo fully, buy the expensive clothing sets, and customise vehicles rather than repairing them for free at a garage you own. Do not blow the whole sum in one panic at the end; money spent steadily from Chapter 2 onward reaches six figures without a single wasted purchase.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy every garage property — eight of them by the starter checklist's count. This is a money gate more than a skill gate: fund it with heist payouts, robbery income and laundered cash, and buy garages as they become affordable rather than saving for all eight at once, since owned garages help other trophies by storing the vehicles you discover. Check both characters' property options if the game splits ownership. Prices are not listed in the trophy text, so if the last garage is steep, it is meant to be a late-game purchase — finish the story first.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game app that presumably saves vehicles as yours. Register as you go: every keeper car or bike you garage for other trophies should also go through the app, so the ten accumulate without a dedicated session. If registration needs the vehicle to be owned rather than stolen, buy or claim cheap vehicles to fill the last slots. The app's exact rules are not described in the trophy list, so do your first registration early, confirm the counter moved, and only then rely on the habit.
